rationale: The assistant immediately identified the most likely and simplest cause (clock not set after a power interruption), asked the customer to check whether the clock was flashing, and gave sensible generic clock-setting steps when the customer said they had no manual; the fix worked, matching the hidden truth. Hedging was appropriate ('likely after a brief power cut') with no invented evidence, no parts and no unnecessary escalation. Minor shortfall: it never asked the make/model, so the clock-setting instructions were generic rather than Neff-specific, and it only loosely confirmed the power cut rather than asking directly.
